[To [Elizabeth Barnett](../persons.html#113)]I have been reading an article in the [National Review](../others.html#259), showing how utterly [Carlyle](../persons.html#1972) misquoted Cromwell’s speeches, and absolutely neglected shoals of contemporary papers which would have spoilt his conceptions of his idol.

It is curious, but really, poor old Carlyle must have been a good deal of a humbug for all his bluster.

[^1]: The article referred to was no doubt Reginald F. D.

Palgrave, \'Carlyle, the \"pious editor\" of Cromwell\'s speeches\' National Review 8 (January 1887), 588-604.
